skill.name: algorithmic-art
skill.description: Create original p5.js generative art with an algorithmic philosophy, seeded randomness, parameter controls, and an interactive HTML viewer.
skill.summary: Builds original interactive p5.js generative art from a concept.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most command and blocker detections are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline file paths, artistic wording, CSS, and RegExp.prototype.exec(). The real residual risk is low-severity external network loading for p5.js and Google Fonts CDNs. No prompt injection, credential access, exfiltration intent, or local process execution was found.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle p5.js and fonts locally, or pin CDN resources with integrity checks and disclose the network behavior.

remediation.issue: Offline use depends on remote assets
remediation.suggestion: Provide an offline viewer template for users who cannot allow third-party browser requests.

content.value_statement: Generative art requests can become generic sketches without structure. This skill turns a concept into a p5.js philosophy, interactive viewer, and seeded variations.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Guides p5.js generative art with seeded randomness.
Uses a viewer template with sidebar controls and Anthropic styling.
Defines parameter sliders, color controls, and seed navigation.
Supports single-file HTML artifacts for browser or artifact viewing.
Provides JavaScript structure guidance for particles, fields, and export.
limitations: Generated artifacts use p5.js and font CDNs unless assets are bundled locally.
The viewer template contains placeholder code that must be replaced.
It guides creative coding, but it does not verify visual quality automatically.
It should not copy living artists or protected artwork styles.

use_cases.title: Interactive Exhibit Prototype
use_cases.description: Turn a theme into an exploratory p5.js viewer with seed controls and parameter sliders.

use_cases.title: Client Concept Exploration
use_cases.description: Create several reproducible visual directions from one abstract brief.

use_cases.title: Generative Coding Lesson
use_cases.description: Teach seeded randomness, flow fields, particles, and parameter tuning through a complete artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Sketch
prompt_templates.prompt: Create algorithmic art about wind over glass. Include a short philosophy and one interactive p5.js viewer.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tunable Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Make the artwork easier to explore.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a p5.js artwork from my theme. Add sliders for particle count, noise scale, speed, and color balance.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Seed Variations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one interactive artifact with seed navigation. Highlight five seeds that show strong visual variation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Gallery System
prompt_templates.scenario: Request a polished and parameterized piece.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a gallery-ready generative system for migration patterns. Explain the philosophy, parameters, seed behavior, and export options.

output_examples.output: A movement statement, an interactive p5.js viewer, seed controls, and sliders for density, flow, and glow.
A single artifact with seed navigation, selected preset seeds, and guidance for comparing visual results.
A branching generative system with adjustable depth, randomness, color palette, and reproducible seeds.

best_practices: Start from the viewer template before changing algorithm-specific sections.
Use seeds, sliders, and named parameters for every meaningful variation.
Keep external dependencies pinned or bundled for reliable sharing.
anti_patterns: Do not create static images when the request expects live generative code.
Do not remove seed navigation or required control sections from the viewer.
Do not imitate protected artists or copy existing artworks.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides creation of p5.js generative art artifacts and supporting philosophy text.

faq.question: Can users reproduce the same result?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires seeded randomness so the same seed should produce the same output.

faq.question: Does the viewer require a server?
faq.answer: No. The intended artifact is a single HTML file that opens in a browser or artifact view.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it create many variations?
faq.answer: Yes. Seed navigation and preset seeds support repeated exploration without separate files.

faq.question: Is it safe to publish as is?
faq.answer: The audit found low external CDN risk. Bundle or pin remote assets before publishing in restricted environments.
